daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

Partai Gelora leader Anis Matta announced the party will campaign for elimination of electoral thresholds, while PSI confirmed it will provide input to DPR on threshold issues in the electoral law. Separately, PSI confirmed that former President Jokowi will assume the position of advisory board chairman, pending a jacket ceremony, though observers noted Jokowi and PSI are still "testing the waters" on the advisory board role. The Constitutional Court has been asked to limit party chairmen terms to a maximum of two periods.

  • The presidential palace responded to student protest demands by claiming the state budget is being economized and promising to evaluate the free nutritious meals program (MBG).
  • Student protesters from Diponegoro University climbed the Central Java governor's office while chanting reformasi slogans, and later announced they will continue demonstrations against the government, citing concerns Indonesia is heading toward crisis.
  • A DPR member proposed the government use the school break to evaluate MBG governance, while another lawmaker urged that the bullying case of a six-year-old in Central Jakarta not be treated as ordinary teenage misconduct.
  • The KPK seized procurement documents related to a corruption case involving the Muara Enim regent.
  • The West Java prosecutor's office named the Indramayu deputy regent a suspect in an alleged corruption case involving DPRD housing allowances.
  • The Ministry of Home Affairs is accelerating village boundary demarcation, with national completion at only 14.4 percent, and is fast-tracking resolution in three Southeast Sulawesi districts.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo met with Japan's defence minister to discuss education and defence technology cooperation. The U.S. Acting Secretary of State Jon Landau visited Jakarta, where Indonesian and American officials highlighted economic ties and Foreign Minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra said the strategic partnership grows on mutual respect. The Indonesian consulate in Penang successfully repatriated three Indonesian toddlers in a humanitarian mission.

  • Indonesia is seeking Brazilian expertise in semiconductors and aerospace.
  • Indonesia sees strong growth potential in trade with Mexico and has launched a cultural center in Mexico City to strengthen bilateral ties.
  • Indonesia highlighted resilience and sustainability at a UN Tourism forum.
  • Indonesia is hosting a Muslim Youth Forum focused on global unity.

Other

The Ministry of Health assured that BPJS medicine prices will not rise despite the weakening rupiah, and separately stated that medicine prices remain within reasonable limits. The government and the INOVASI partnership are working to strengthen literacy in Nusantara, while Muhammadiyah announced it will build an infusion factory at UMM that will begin operations in 2027. Commission VI of the DPR will summon Pertamina to discuss the impact of Pertamax price increases.

  • Pertamina said Pertalite supply is stable nationwide, though police arrested a Medan resident for buying 25 liters of Pertalite, with the individual facing a potential Rp 60 billion fine.
  • A deputy minister said food security is key to economic transformation, while officials directed local leaders to temporarily close food barns (SPPG) that do not absorb local farmer and livestock commodities, with 400 SPPG in Central Java halted due to stalled fund disbursements.
  • Indonesia plans to renovate 71,744 schools in 2026, though West Java Governor Dedi Mulyadi admitted mistakes after parents protested the student admission system and promised free schooling for those who did not pass into state schools.
  • Indonesia is mapping out regional retail hubs to boost shopping tourism and is strengthening its quarantine system to boost exports.
  • Indonesia welcomed a new ILO convention protecting gig workers, with the Manpower Minister also welcoming the ILC's adoption of decent work standards for platform workers.
